Trauma often has lasting effects, impacting a person life as well as identity. For survivors of trafficking and forced exploitation, the path to recovery from the immense trauma they endured is fraught with challenges, including psychological distress, societal stigma, and the constant struggle to rebuild trust and reclaim a sense of normalcy. However, dealing with such highly challenging life situations can also result in a positive and meaningful development known as post-traumatic growth. Changes due to post-traumatic growth can manifest as personal strength, discovery of new possibilities, appreciation of life, improved relationships, and spiritual and existential growth. Experiencing trauma deepens empathy and compassion, fuelling determination and passion for change. As Firoja Khatun, a survivor leader, reflects, the traumatic incident, turning around from there, and not wanting others to be in that place of hurt this journey stays with us. The cognitive process of grappling with existential questions, interpreting the trauma, finding meaning in suffering, and the creation of emotional and social support structures during recovery supports the emergence of post-traumatic growth. A study in October, 2024 by Kamonohashi Project with a Kolkata company involved 60 survivors from five survivor collectives in West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh. The participants have been working on developing their leadership capacities since 2018 as part of the Leadership Next programme. The findings revealed that 98 percent of the respondents reported experiencing moderate to high levels of post-traumatic growth. Based on the study, we detail how leadership fosters post-traumatic growth, the challenges faced by the survivors in this process, and the steps that organisations can take to maximise their impact in nurturing survivor leadership, sustaining growth, and enabling systemic and communitydriven changes. Post-traumatic growth is a long journey. Many survivors continue to seek external validation, struggle with sustained motivation, and face interpersonal challenges. These issues may stem from deep-seated trauma and unhealed emotional wounds. A stronger focus on goal- or action-driven mentorship often leads to limited attention to internal and collective healing and growth. This highlights the need for a holistic approach in leadership development one that integrates internal and external growth at the self, collective, community, and systemic levels, while also being goal-driven. A holistic approach includes continued emotional guidance and trauma-informed support using interventions essential for healing and growth. The programme should help survivors rebuild their self-worth and support them in fostering healthy relationships through conflict resolution and trust-building. Nonprofits should support their relational and collective growth, strengthening leadership at all levels. Here how they can do so. The design of the leadership programme should prioritise the survivors voice by asking, what do you want to do? This simple yet profound question becomes a catalyst for selfdetermination, which is critical for leadership development. Engaging learners with a different pace of learning is not easy. For learners to be engaged, it is crucial to comprehend how the human brain works during the learning process. This has made teachers more eager than ever in recent years to use research on the brain to direct their work in the classroom. Consequently, finding a workable approach to integrate scientific knowledge in teaching and learning has necessitated neuroeducation. Neuroeducation is all about creating, implementing, and experimenting with new approaches to maximise student learning in the classroom. It studies the brain underpinnings of reading, mathematical cognition, and attention and the educational challenges related to learning abilities, such as dyslexia, dyscalculia, and ADHD. It makes teaching practises more informed by integrating the most recent discoveries in neuroscience, psychology, and cognitive science. It is backed by proven research that the brain has adaptive ability across its lifecycle, mirror neurons enable mimicking and comprehension of the actions around us, emotional excitement promotes durable learning and that stimulation of the five senses makes the brain more able. Designing curricula and teaching methods using the scientific method accompanied by efforts to develop a more fact-based, objective understanding of learning is the purpose of this emerging field. Role in transforming education Neuroeducation demonstrates the significance of sleep, healthy diet, exercising and variation in education for functions like memory formation, retention, enhancement of cognitive capacities and effective learning. It can transform education in the following ways- Individualised learning Personalised learning experience for each student is one of the cornerstones of neuroscience. It will help in overcoming challenges related to learning. And eventually, it might become possible to demonstrate more selfcontrol attributable to the revelation that the brain possesses systems for self-regulation. An adaptive and socially motivating environment Conventional teaching techniques, like live lectures, one-size-fits-all instruction, testing based on memory, etc., have all come under the scrutiny of neuroeducation. A neuroeducation-enabled environment is adaptive to the needs of learners and helps in better comprehending social and emotional intelligence, a must in the well-being of children, to enable stronger emotional intelligence in subsequent generations. It also promotes obstacles and incentives to stimulate brain regions that support learning. Dynamic learning It encourages brainstimulating and synaptic-building activities, including music, memory games, and practical thinking exercises. It promotes short and diverse lessons and identifies that long training sessions and too much information overload the memory, which makes learning difficult. It promotes arts training which benefits learning in all areas, including cognitive, emotional, and social abilities. Additionally, it encourages incremental acquisition of information rather than everything at once to increase understanding and the development of new neurons. In today generation, where traditions and "customs often intertwine" with modern lifestyles, Karwa Chauth continues to hold a special place in the hearts of married couples. This auspicious Hindu festival, predominantly celebrated by women, showcases a beautiful blend of tradition and the evolving dynamics of relationships. Karwa Chauth is a day-long fast observed by married women for the well-being and longevity of their husbands. While fasting from sunrise to moonrise can be physically demanding, it symbolizes the deep love, commitment, and sacrifice that wives are willing to make for their spouses. However, in today fast-paced world, the significance of Karwa Chauth has taken on a new meaning. It no longer just about the fasting ritual, but also about celebrating the bond between partners and embracing the essence of togetherness. The digital age has also played a significant role, as technology allows couples to stay connected throughout the day, despite physical distances. Video calls, messages, and virtual celebrations have become the norm, ensuring that the essence of Karwa Chauth is preserved even when couples are apart. In the modern world, some feminists express opposition to Karwa Chauth, viewing it as a patriarchal tradition that reinforces gender roles and inequality. They argue that the festival places undue pressure on women to prioritize the well-being of their husbands above their own needs and aspirations. Critics argue that fasting for the longevity of husbands perpetuates the idea that a woman worth is tied solely to her marital status and her ability to fulfill traditional gender roles. They advocate for redefining relationships based on equality and mutual respect, rather than subscribing to traditional norms upheld by festivals like Karwa Chauth. In conclusion, Karwa Chauth remains a deeply cherished and significant festival for many married Hindu women, celebrating love, devotion, and the bonds of marriage. While it may attract differing opinions and critiques, its continued observance highlights the richness and diversity of cultural practices in our modern world. Whether one chooses to participate in Karwa Chauth or not, the festival serves as a reminder of the enduring traditions and evolving dynamics within relationships. It is through open dialogue and understanding that we can appreciate and respect the various perspectives surrounding Karwa Chauth and other cultural celebrations. Drainage design and lack of regular upkeep lead to unforeseen water torrents in the cities. For systematic run-off, the water should be directed through a planned network of storm water drains designed according to regional rainfall patterns in the urban area. Ensuring Water Percolation The modernization of cities alters their natural topography and water run-off patterns due to non-permeable hard surfaces like roads, pavements, plazas, etc., compromising groundwater percolation. Therefore, such spaces should have substantial perforations in the form of green spaces and soil cover that allow for water seepage and prevent overflow. Moreover, parking lots designed in commercial spaces can have perforated paver blocks that allow water to be soaked into the earth. Generally, building roofs catch rainwater which is diverted to drains and contribute to the overflowing water in the streets. Green roofs can solve this problem by absorbing up to 80 percent of the rain that falls onto them. Trees also do their bit in lessening the impact of floods. Their roots can help reduce storm water run-off by absorbing rainwater and improving storm water filters through the ground. Trapping Excess Water Floods are the result of excess water which is not channelized systematically. On a neigbourhood level, local parks can have a better landscape design with water features like ponds that act as natural water catchments in monsoons. Monsoon rainwater run-offs can be harnessed to conserve this water with the help of reservoirs and bios wales. Such a planned water channel network does just prevent flooding but can also help conserve water for potable use. Planning For Rivers Human disturbance of local water bodies such as lakes, ponds, rivers, etc., is also a major reason for flooding in urban areas. Building activities and encroachment on river banks disturb these water bodies by introducing hard surfaces, which hinders the water seepage. Such actions are one of the significant causes of overflowing rivers during monsoon season. This problem can be tackled on an urban scale. For example, if a river runs on a city outskirts, interventions can enable protection from flooding by water diversions like streams, canals and other means to channelize the excess flow of water. In case a water body exists within a city fabric, one solution can be to create embankments, which are large walls constructed as an interface between the city and the river. Spillover reservoirs are also constructed as an alternative to take up surplus water during heavy rains. Such design ideas can be used at urban and community levels, which not only help in designing flood-resilient cities but also allow for a systematic utilization of water. Wherever it been tried in our country, Many marine organisms rely on their ability to hear for their survival. Sound is a highly efficient means of communication underwater and is the primary way that many marine species gather and understand information about their environment. Many aquatic animals use sound to find prey locate mates and offspring avoid predators guide their navigation and locate habitat as well as to listen and communicate with each other. Oceans are full of sound. Waves, earthquakes and icebergs - all contribute to the underwater soundscape. But so do human activities and this can be a problem for marine life as it can seriously affect their physiology behaviour, reproduction and even survival. Being able to produce and detect sound in an environment where light penetrates only a few hundred meters is crucial for animals to communicate, feed, avoid predators and navigate vast underwater habitats. Many navies use sonar system to detect ships and submarines while geologists survey the seabed for oil and gas using seismic air guns. The noise produced by an air gun can exceed 200 decibels louder than a gunshot at a range of one meter. Sound travels further and four times faster in water than in air at a speed of almost 1500 meters per second. The noise produced by humans can therefore spread considerable distances underwater. These sounds can be relatively constant such as the noise produced by the engine of a ship and propeller or sudden and acute in the case of naval sonar and seismic air guns. Kidney disease is caused by the same dietary and lifestyle factors that contribute to these conditions, and it is often worsened by the medications prescribed to treat them. If, instead of relying on medication, you manage these conditions through diet and lifestyle changes, you are far less likely to develop kidney disease. Research clearly shows that animal protein and animal fat play a significant role in kidney health decline. The protein myth and its impact on kidney health The human body is highly efficient at conserving protein, recycling about 85% of its daily. This means that very little new protein is required each day. However, due to widespread misconceptions about protein intake, people tend to consume excessive amounts, particularly from animal sources. When we consume more protein than our body needs, the excess must be converted into fat. This process involves removing nitrogen from the protein structure. Aside from nitrogen, proteins, fats, and carbohydrates are all composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. The nitrogen released during protein metabolism combines with hydrogen to form ammonia The kidneys perform a vital function: filtering toxins and waste from the blood. In addition, they help regulate electrolyte balance, fluid levels, and acid-base balance in the body. A healthy kidney filters about 6 liters of blood per hour, producing approximately 60 milliliters of urine. When the kidneys fail, dialysis becomes necessary. Unfortunately, dialysis has become one of the fastest-growing industries today, with dialysis centers appearing in shopping centers everywhere. One major reason for this rise is our obsession with protein consumption, as highlighted by Dr. Janice Stanger in her video The Dangerous Truth About Protein. Another factor is our overreliance on medications. Every medication we take must be processed by the liver and kidneys, placing an additional burden on these organs. Since kidney damage results from toxic exposure to processed foods, animal products, alcohol, tobacco, and medications, the best approach is to eliminate these harmful substances and restore kidney function naturally. The latest example is Nepal, where the earthquake and its tragic aftermath have been exploited to the hilt by television cameras in an appalling race for TRPs. The role of the media during disasters is an important one. Before a catastrophe, they can warn a population and prepare it. Afterwards, with continued reportage, they can ensure that no survivor is forgotten or left out of the aid network. But it is during the disaster that their role is quite vital. They can be effective conduits of information about help lines, aiddistribution camps, emergency phone numbers, or the kind of supplies required. They can help scotch rumors and prevent panic by quickly disseminating the right facts and figures. Their coverage helps mobilize help from outside the disaster area, in the form of money, supplies and volunteers. And finally, the focus of the media on a disaster helps increase its visibility, thus forcing governments to upgrade it on their agenda. While India s television crews did most of this, they were overstepping the boundaries so often and so dramatically that the Nepalese people finally turned against them and virtually asked them to leave. This was unfortunate, given that Indian rescue teams were indeed the first to reach Nepal and have played a stellar role there, as did the media in sending out some of the first images of the calamity. But it is imperative that television revisits the basic rules of journalistic ethics during disaster reporting. Regardless of how important they imagine it is to wring an emotional response from audiences, they must refrain from sticking microphones in the faces of survivors who may have just lost everything. People s right to know just does not apply here. Nobody has a right to know how much anyone else is grieving. Instead, it is the survivor who has an absolute right to privacy. Leaders need to be aware of this and build strong relationships inside and outside the workplace to counteract these effects. Investing time in building connections with peers and seeking out mentors can be critical in avoiding the loneliness trap. Who actually in control? In the intricate dance of the global economy, two formidable forces vie for dominance: tech monopolies and regulatory bodies. This dynamic interplay shapes markets, influences innovation, and determines the balance of power between private enterprise and public interest. Over the past two decades, technology companies have experienced unprecedented growth, with some achieving market capitalizations exceeding $1 trillion. Firms like Amazon, Google, and Apple have become integral to daily life, offering services that range from online shopping to information retrieval and communication. Their expansive reach has led to concerns about monopolistic behaviors, including stifling competition and exploiting market dominance. For instance, the European Commission imposed antitrust fines totaling 8.25 billion on Google between 2017 and 2024 for abusing its market position. Tech companies like Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet Google, Amazon, and Meta Facebook are no longer just businesses; they are economies unto themselves. Their market capitalizations have skyrocketed, their profits are staggering, and their control over data, infrastructure, and consumer behavior is virtually absolute. The crux of the debate lies in finding a balance between fostering innovations and preventing monopolistic practices. Excessive regulation may stifle technological advancement, while insufficient oversight can lead to market abuses. For example, despite increased antitrust cases and new regulations, companies like Amazon and Google have effectively neutralized these challenges, maintaining their dominant positions. Conversely, unchecked monopolies can hinder competition, reduce consumer choices, and concentrate economic power. The challenge for regulators is to craft policies that promote fair competition without discouraging the entrepreneurial spirit that drives technological progress. Who Holds the Reins? The global economy trajectory is influenced by the continuous interplay between tech monopolies and regulatory authorities. Figures like Elon Musk illustrate the dual-edged nature of technological dominance capable of driving innovation while posing challenges to equitable market practices. Ultimately, achieving a harmonious balance requires adaptive regulations that safeguard public interests without impeding the transformative potential of technology. The brutal truth? Tech monopolies are more powerful than governments when it comes to shaping the modern economy. While lawmakers argue in committee hearings, these corporations dictate consumer behavior, control infrastructure, and wield economic influence at a level never seen before. Regulation may slow these monopolies, but it won stop them. The global economy is just influenced by Big Tech; it is practically owned by it. Until governments find a way to outmaneuver corporations that are richer, faster, and more technologically advanced, the true rulers of the global economy will sit in Silicon Valley boardrooms, not in presidential offices or parliamentary halls. Bone pain in CML usually affects large and long bones like the sternum, shoulder bones, bones of the legs, and hands due to their increased bone marrow density. Causes of CML is caused by spontaneous chromosome mutation, which causes pathogenic white blood cells to proliferate in large numbers, crowding out healthy blood cells and causing bone marrow damage. The mutated gene BCR-ABL is responsible for CML, and this produces a high number of immature white blood cells which leads to several symptoms in the patients. Management & Treatment Continuous monitoring of CML is extremely essential. It allows the doctor to administer the proper dose and therefore keep the issue in check. A complete blood count CBC is utilized for monitoring, typically to assess the white blood cell count. When the illness is first diagnosed, monitoring should be done every three months, and thereafter every six months. While these are the recommended periods, the frequency of monitoring is partly determined by the circumstances of each case. The manifestation of symptoms of CML like bone pain will also subside in patients if they adhere to regular checks, tests, and monitoring of the condition. It is important to follow the doctor advice. failure to follow treatment methods can cause the condition to deteriorate and may exacerbate bone pain as a result. Hence, patients should not break their treatment cycles and stay in touch with their healthcare providers. In terms of treatment, patients should remember that CML is not a deadly disease and that with the right kind of treatment choices, patients have a normal life expectancy. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors TKIs are the first-line treatment for most patients with CML, and more than two-thirds of patients obtain long-term disease control with them. AIIMS (All India Institute of Medical Sciences) is one of the premier medical institutes in India, known for its high standards of education, research, and healthcare. The AIIMS entrance exams, particularly for postgraduate and undergraduate courses, are highly competitive and require extensive preparation. Among the key tools that students rely on during their preparation for the AIIMS exams are the AIIMS CRE (Clinical Reasoning Exercise) notes. What are AIIMS CRE Notes? AIIMS CRE notes are a set of study materials designed to help students prepare for the AIIMS exams, especially for the clinical reasoning sections. The CRE section focuses on assessing a candidate ability to apply medical knowledge to clinical scenarios, making it a crucial part of the examination. This is particularly important for those aiming to enter AIIMS postgraduate programs, such as MD/MS, where clinical decision-making is a key skill. The CRE notes typically contain a combination of theoretical knowledge, clinical case discussions, diagnostic strategies, and treatment plans. These notes are structured in a way that helps students improve their diagnostic thinking, clinical skills, and overall understanding of medical science. The clinical reasoning section assesses a student ability to critically analyze complex patient scenarios, which is why having a comprehensive set of notes is vital for success. Why is AIIMS CRE Notes Important? 1. Comprehensive Understanding the CRE notes covers a broad range of medical conditions, from common to rare ones. This helps students develop a deeper understanding of diseases, their pathophysiology, symptoms, and treatment protocols. The notes guide students to think through cases step by step, understanding the clinical manifestations and investigative procedures, which are essential for diagnosis and management. 2. Critical Thinking and Analytical Skills AIIMS exams, particularly the CRE section, are designed to test a candidate ability to think critically. CRE notes often contain clinical scenarios that require students to analyze the information, differentiate between possible diagnoses, and choose the most appropriate treatment. These notes hone the analytical skills that students will need not just for exams but for practical medical practice. 3. Exam-Oriented Approach Since the AIIMS exams are highly competitive, students need to prepare in an exam-focused manner. AIIMS CRE notes are structured according to the exam pattern and syllabus. They contain the key topics, highyield points, and clinical cases that are frequently tested. This focused preparation helps students maximize their performance and tackle even the most difficult cases presented in the exam. 4. Time Management The CRE section requires quick thinking and efficient time management. With extensive practice using CRE notes, students can become familiar with how to manage time during the exam, which is crucial to solving the case studies efficiently. These notes often include time-saving tips and mnemonic devices, which help students, retain complex information in a shorter period. 5. Guidance from Experts CRE notes are typically written by medical experts, specialists, or educators who have experience in teaching and preparing students for AIIMS exams. This ensures that the content is not only accurate but also aligned with the current examination trends.
